new_targets.why: n8n is the dominant self-hosted workflow automation platform (203,618★, 400+ integrations, active enterprise user base). Its AI Agent nodes — introduced in late 2024 — dispatch tool calls (HTTP request, code execution, external API calls) after LLM output parsing with no per-agent identity gate. Because n8n positions its AI Agents as production-ready for financial and regulated workflows, the absence of an identity binding at tool dispatch is felt directly by enterprise teams. A Bolyra EVC verifier as an n8n credential-type or a pre-tool hook in the AI Agent node reaches every tool call in every AI workflow across the platform. This is the highest-star target identified in 10 weeks of scanning.
new_targets.gap: n8n's AI Agent node (packages/nodes-base/nodes/Agent/) dispatches LLM-selected tools directly after parsing the tool-call output. There is no pre-invocation hook to verify caller identity or mandate. An optional 'Bolyra Authorization' credential type that triggers an EVC check before each tool invocation closes the gap — implemented as a new credential type plus a short pre-execution hook in the AI Agent node. Non-breaking: workflows without the credential run exactly as today.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search n8n-io/n8n issues for 'agent authorization', 'tool guard', 'access control', or 'identity'. n8n community.n8n.io may also surface demand. The repo has a CONTRIBUTING.md and active maintainers.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — new Bolyra credential type + optional pre-tool EVC check in AI Agent node. Keep the diff to the agent node package and one credential file. A companion example workflow JSON in examples/ demonstrates the integration.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry points: packages/nodes-base/nodes/Agent/ for the AI Agent node; packages/nodes-base/credentials/ for credential types. n8n uses pnpm workspaces and strict TypeScript. Run pnpm build:nodes before submitting. Tests in packages/nodes-base/test/. n8n has an external contributors guide; a linked community post asking for demand feedback before the PR reduces merge risk.

new_targets.why: This is the x402-foundation canonical protocol repo (6,582★, 508 open issues, active) — distinct from coinbase/x402 identified in week 6, which is Coinbase's implementation. The foundation repo defines the facilitator verification reference and is used as the spec-level implementation. The facilitator currently verifies settlement validity (correct token, amount, recipient) but has no concept of agent identity — any valid payment claim passes regardless of which agent submitted it. A Bolyra mandate hook in the facilitator's verification path would close the gap at the protocol reference layer, shaping all downstream x402 implementations.
new_targets.gap: The facilitator's verifyPayment() function (packages/typescript/src/facilitators/) checks settlement correctness but makes no claim about caller identity. An optional bolyra_mandate field in the x402 payment payload, verified by the facilitator before accepting the payment, binds each payment to a specific agent mandate. The fix is additive: facilitators that don't enable the Bolyra check are unaffected; those that do can enforce per-agent spend limits and delegation.
new_targets.anchor_issue: x402-foundation/x402 has 508 open issues — search for 'agent identity', 'authorization', 'mandate', 'who sent this', or 'caller'. Agent-to-agent payment traceability is a live discussion in the x402 community.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — optional bolyra_mandate field in the PaymentPayload type plus a reference verifier hook in the facilitator. Ships as an optional extension — existing facilitators unaffected. TypeScript strict, reference implementation only.
new_targets.builder_notes: Entry point: packages/typescript/src/facilitators/ — study existing verifyPayment() implementation. The repo uses pnpm + TypeScript strict. Check CONTRIBUTING.md for DCO requirements. The foundation repo has very active maintainers (508 issues, updated yesterday) — a well-scoped PR with a clear 'why' will be reviewed quickly.

new_targets.why: ruflo (71,179★) is 'the original agent meta-harness' — deploying multi-agent swarms, coordinating autonomous workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Agents in a swarm share the operator-level identity with no scope narrowing; a spawned sub-agent inherits full tool access with no delegation gate. ruflo's skills system (the designed extension point) makes a BolyraAuthSkill the cleanest non-core injection path. The claude-code and codex topics signal alignment with the developer-tool tier Bolyra targets; the harness's MCP integration means Bolyra's EVC verifier can gate MCP tool calls across the swarm.
new_targets.gap: ruflo's swarm tool dispatch (the harness loop that dispatches MCP tool calls to agents) has no identity gate between the swarm orchestrator and individual agents. An agent requesting a high-permission tool call (financial, PII) gets through on the operator key alone. A BolyraAuthSkill in the skills system — evaluated before any tool call dispatched by the harness — closes the gap and can enforce the delegation scope narrows-only invariant across agent hierarchies.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search ruvnet/ruflo issues for 'authorization', 'permission', 'scope', or 'identity'. The repo is actively developed; ruvnet is a single-maintainer project with fast response times on focused PRs.
new_targets.pr_type: contrib skill — BolyraAuthSkill in a new skills/bolyra/ directory, implementing the harness skill interface. Verifies a Bolyra mandate before tool dispatch. Zero change to harness core. Companion example in examples/bolyra-auth-swarm/ showing a delegation hierarchy across agents.
new_targets.builder_notes: Study the harness skill interface (from skills/ directory) before writing BolyraAuthSkill. ruflo uses pnpm, TypeScript. Run existing skill tests before adding a new one. The maintainer merges skill contributions quickly — keep the PR scoped to the skill + example + README.md in the skill directory.

new_targets.why: nanobot (47,834★) is an ultra-lightweight self-hosted personal AI agent framework from Hong Kong University of Science — MCP, tools, multi-agent workflows, WebUI, Discord/Telegram bots. Tool dispatch runs with operator identity and no per-agent gate. The openclaw topic (also used by bolyra's integrations/openclaw/) is a strong signal that maintainers value protocol integrations. Academic provenance means maintainers are receptive to well-reasoned security/identity contributions. At 47k★ it reaches a large self-hosted community — enterprise and privacy-focused users who are exactly the audience that cares about per-agent authorization.
new_targets.gap: nanobot's tool execution pipeline (the bot plugin/tool dispatch loop) runs registered tools with operator-level identity. There is no authorization hook between 'LLM requested tool X' and 'tool X executes'. An optional bolyra_auth_callback parameter on the nanobot Agent (or a BolyraAuthPlugin in the plugin system) — evaluated before each tool invocation — closes the gap without touching core behavior.
new_targets.anchor_issue: Search HKUDS/nanobot issues for 'authorization', 'tool guard', 'access control', or 'permission'. At 771 open issues, demand signals are likely already present.
new_targets.pr_type: targeted feature — optional bolyra_auth_callback on Agent plus a BolyraAuthPlugin contrib in a plugins/bolyra/ directory. Non-breaking: absent callback runs exactly as today. Python strict typing, follows existing plugin patterns.
new_targets.builder_notes: Study the existing plugin architecture (plugins/ directory) before writing BolyraAuthPlugin. Python 3.10+, uses ruff + mypy. Add a test in tests/test_bolyra_auth_plugin.py. The CONTRIBUTING.md (if it exists) will have style requirements. The MCP integration in nanobot makes this doubly relevant — Bolyra can gate MCP tool calls specifically.

new_targets.why: CowAgent (46,802★, formerly chatgpt-on-wechat, 10k+ forks) is a high-adoption multi-channel AI agent and harness deployed across WeChat, Slack, DingTalk, Telegram, email. It has a plugin tool dispatch system, MCP integration, and — crucially — the openclaw topic in a 46k★ repo, signaling deliberate alignment with the openclaw ecosystem that Bolyra integrates with (integrations/openclaw/). The multi-channel deployment model means tool calls may originate from any connected channel; binding each call to an agent identity is precisely the trust problem Bolyra solves.
new_targets.gap: CowAgent's tool/skill plugin dispatch (the plugin manager executing tool requests from the LLM) runs with operator identity and no caller gate. A BolyraToolPlugin that wraps the plugin dispatch loop — verifying a Bolyra mandate before executing any tool call — closes the gap. The plugin interface is the designed extension point; this is a contrib plugin, not a core change.
